completed_task_notes.NEX-039: The first real DecisionProvider adapter, so decisioning stops being a capability the platform can exercise but never use. Product commit 8e670a6, CI 4/4 completed/success at that exact SHA (polled 2026-11-25T19:32Z). Four refusals carry the security argument: a vendor cannot abstain (no 'abstained' outcome on the wire; the caller's threshold decides), the request carries only kind plus sorted candidates (no context hash, no excluded field names, no correlation id), sorting makes order-independence a property of this adapter rather than a hoped-for vendor trait, and a bad answer is an abstention rather than an exception. Construction fails closed on a non-https endpoint or an unbounded name. Two honest limits are recorded in the module docstring: the response size bound is enforced after httpx has read the body, and a rationale is truncated rather than treated as fatal.

run_summary: Implemented NEX-056: the `rate-limit` obligation got its enforcement adapter. It was the third of five named obligations with no mechanism - the gateway refused every call a policy placed it on, which is honest but left the policy language unable to express a volume bound at all. The adapter reuses the `RateLimiter` port the HTTP boundary already depends on, keyed per agent AND per tool so a hot tool cannot exhaust the budget of every other tool the same agent may call. An idempotent retry does not consume budget (a replay of a recorded decision is not a new call), and a refusal is audited as a denial naming the retry window. Enforcement runs before the approval gate so a flood cannot fill the approval queue. Still fails closed with no limiter wired, which is why the old 'unsatisfiable' test survives in a no-limiter harness. Gates: ruff format 291 files, ruff check clean, mypy 138 files, pytest 1308 passed / 4 skipped. Pushed as e7c7315 and CI polled to 4/4 completed/success. This run also cleared run 56's delivery debt: NEX-054 and NEX-055 sections appended to PR #5 (21968 chars, 33 files) and a NEX-054/055/056 status comment posted to issue #2 (7225253883). Delivery finished: docs commit f7a085b pushed and remote-verified, PR #5 CI-evidence comment posted (7225324419), and CI on the docs head polled to 4/4 success.

decisions_this_run: D-056: the rate-limit bound is deployment configuration, not policy vocabulary. A rule says 'a volume bound applies'; the operator sets the number. A per-rule bound would need a parameterised PolicyObligation - a vocabulary change and therefore an ADR.

D-057: rate-limit is checked before approval, not after. A caller already over budget must be refused before it can open an approval request, otherwise a flood fills the human approval queue with requests that can never be used.
